title: Global Spaceports & Launch Sites
metadata: Primary active orbital spaceports and rocket launch facilities around the world.
Showcasing isListEnabled set to false (pure map experience with bottom drawer disabled), aggressive optimization enabled, and agency-coded marker colors.

records.title: Kennedy Space Center & Cape Canaveral
records.description: United States - NASA's primary human spaceflight launch facility and the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Home to historic Apollo Saturn V, Space Shuttle, and modern Artemis/SpaceX Falcon 9 and Heavy launches.

records.title: Vandenberg Space Force Base
records.description: United States (California) - The premier West Coast spaceport, specializing in polar, Sun-synchronous, and high-inclination orbital insertions over the open Pacific Ocean.

records.title: Guiana Space Centre (CSG)
records.description: French Guiana - Europe's Spaceport operated jointly by CNES and ESA. Located just 5.3 degrees north of the Equator, maximizing the rotational assist of Earth for geostationary launches with Ariane and Vega rockets.

records.title: Baikonur Cosmodrome
records.description: Kazakhstan - The world's first and largest operational space launch facility. Launched Sputnik 1 in 1957 and Yuri Gagarin on Vostok 1 in 1961; ongoing staging ground for Soyuz crewed missions to the ISS.

records.title: Tanegashima Space Center (TNSC)
records.description: Japan (Kagoshima Prefecture) - JAXA's primary rocket launch site situated on the southeastern coast of Tanegashima island, known as one of the most picturesque coastal spaceports in the world.

records.title: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR)
records.description: India (Sriharikota Island, Andhra Pradesh) - ISRO's main orbital launch centre, responsible for Chandrayaan lunar missions, Mangalyaan Mars mission, and PSLV/LVM3 satellite launches.

records.title: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1
records.description: New Zealand (Mahia Peninsula) - The world's first private commercial orbital launch facility, dedicated to Rocket Lab Electron missions with high orbital launch cadence.

records.title: Esrange Space Center
records.description: Sweden (Kiruna) - Arctic rocket range operated by the Swedish Space Corporation. Inaugurated Spaceport Esrange for orbital satellite launches in 2023.
